ILLEGAL MINING | SEWER TOURS

By: Hein Kaiser | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We investigate the dangers that Zama Zamas pose to Gauteng and look into how this phenomenon created it’s own micro economy

Unique Selling Point:
Nobody has exposed the intricacies of the Zama Zama world before, instead focusing on their mining. There is much more to this, including pending danger.

Summary:
We investigate the burrowing below Johannesburg. Can the city implode ? Are they under your home right now?

And then we look at how every area where Zamas operate has changed. From geology to economy. It’s a tour of the dangerous underground world.

We explore the sewers underneath Johannesburg and a source reveals how everything is interconnected, how the Zamas have tunnelled their way under Johannesburg… and a geologist tells us that this is one of the biggest risks that Johannesburg and Ekurhuleni faces - more sinkholes, more implosions. Potential disaster.

And that’s as if the Zamas are not doing enough damage already. They are costing the country billions annually in revenues, yet they have created their own micro economy.

Where there are Zamas. There is money. From the opens air bush meat butchery and Zama restaurant through to the formal and informal businesses they support. The Zama economy is real, and is it a bad thing ?

But violence, turf wars, the hollowing out of the city…. Is the risk worth the reward?

Further information:
ZAMA Treatment



Visuals:

I would like to create a highly visual, scary scenario at first, but bring in the absolute danger element with guns, lookouts, the sickening (see butchery) and then the gold that it becomes.

I feel it must be fast paced, visually – and have a “blood diamonds” feel to it, for a lack of a better term… because in a sense, that is what this is becoming.

And then…

An introduction of buildings collapsing and giant gaping wounds in roads (SFX where possible) … this could be large cities along the reef, and it may happen sooner than we think.

After all, sinkholes because of mining activity are nothing new, neither are tremors.

There are around 25-40 000 Zama Zamas operating across a stretch of about 100km east to West.

And we have seen the decay as a consequence of their activities happen all around us.

…. It’s a highly visual piece with exploration of the entire world of Zama’s – from the massive threat that they now pose to infrastructure across the province through to the social (already covered by Chuma but to be touched on slightly) consequences, safety risks and the recent factional fighting in Riverlea.

We look at the massive threat that uncontrolled mining could have on the city.

- Underground tunnelling systems hollowing out Johannesburg.
- Use of sewers and old tunnels to interconnect (beneath the gas pipelines)
- The Zama shafts, quarries, and warrens, some right under major roads
- The Sasol / FNB Study referencing the pipelines at FNB (still need to film the Zamas there)
- A Geologist will say that it’s not the illicit gold that is the problem, it is the massive risk to infrastructure.
- And we can show that the risk / danger is real. In a single 50sqm spot, at least 12 shafts were dug, in other areas, it’s beneath main thoroughfares. We can show how Eloff Street Extension wobbled because the ground below has become unstable…
- Marius and Cobus (in rushes) will guide us with additional commentary, almost like guides along with the presenter, to the various Zama spots and into the sewers (up to a safe point).
- Can we control/rein in the Zamas? With around 20 000 SAPS and Metro Police members across the province, law enforcement is outnumbered.

But how did the Zamas become such a massive force? It’s the power of money. And a value chain that operates outside of the economy.

- We will learn about the two major factions, the Basotho’s, and the Zulus. Their war (Riverlea is an example).
- We see how Zamas surface mine and wash their loot.
- We visit a Zama processing plant where pandukas process the raw washed rocks, grinds them into sand. And then packaged and sold on to the next tier in the chain. But we will speak to the Zimbabwean national who runs this operation, and he will reveal some of his clients and how his portion of the chain works.
- The “sand” is then carted off to one of the many refineries on the East Rand… here it is mixed with legitimate gold and thus, “washed clean” and flows into the bullion system. A former manager at a refinery in Benoni will detail this for us.



Also – who buys this gold? We endeavour to answer that question…..


An independent Zama can produce up to 3g of gold a day, and dependent on the market price, can earn R 900 – R 1500 per gram. At 7 days a week and an average of 2g a day, it is a substantial amount.

And apart from the money that the expats, many illegal, send home. They have spending power. And entire micro economies have grown around them.

- The Zama Butchery and Braai, an open area where meat (cattle, bush meat etc) is grilled on old burning tyres.
- The rows and rows of vendors selling Zama materials – from plastic buckets through to spades etc,
- The entrepreneurs who make pandukas in industrial areas…



The People

- Marius and Cobus
- “Smurf” – a Zama fixer
- “Greg” – former refinery manager
- Letwelo – Geologist at engineering firm Bulwark Consulting Engineers
- “Brandon” – Zimbabwean second tier processor
- Vox Pops with willing Zamas
- Possible confront with Gold One (JSE), allegedly guilty of buying Zama gold. But I need to film the evidence of this if we can get close enough without being shot.

text: Add New Proposal Shows Add New Show View All Shows 17 May 2026 - Carte Blanche HD 10 May 2026 - Carte Blanche HD 03 May 2026 - Carte Blanche HD 26 April 2026 - Carte Blanche HD 19 April 2026 - Carte Blanche HD 12 April 2026 - Carte Blanche HD 05 April 2026 - Carte Blanche HD Hi Lezanne [My Account] [Logout] Home Viewer Submissions Reports Contacts Music Cue Sheet Manage Users View Insert Edit Insert Insert Workflow ILLEGAL MINING | SEWER TOURS By: Hein Kaiser | Paid Proposal Show: Carte Blanche One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We investigate the dangers that Zama Zamas pose to Gauteng and look into how this phenomenon created it’s own micro economy Unique Selling Point: Nobody has exposed the intricacies of the Zama Zama world before, instead focusing on their mining. There is much more to this, including pending danger. Summary: We investigate the burrowing below Johannesburg. Can the city implode ? Are they under your home right now? And then we look at how every area where Zamas operate has changed. From geology to economy. It’s a tour of the dangerous underground world. We explore the sewers underneath Johannesburg and a source reveals how everything is interconnected, how the Zamas have tunnelled their way under Johannesburg… and a geologist tells us that this is one of the biggest risks that Johannesburg and Ekurhuleni faces - more sinkholes, more implosions. Potential disaster. And that’s as if the Zamas are not doing enough damage already. They are costing the country billions annually in revenues, yet they have created their own micro economy. Where there are Zamas. There is money. From the opens air bush meat butchery and Zama restaurant through to the formal and informal businesses they support. The Zama economy is real, and is it a bad thing ? But violence, turf wars, the hollowing out of the city…. Is the risk worth the reward? Further information: ZAMA Treatment Visuals: I would like to create a highly visual, scary scenario at first, but bring in the absolute danger element with guns, lookouts, the sickening (see butchery) and then the gold that it becomes. I feel it must be fast paced, visually – and have a “blood diamonds” feel to it, for a lack of a better term… because in a sense, that is what this is becoming. And then… An introduction of buildings collapsing and giant gaping wounds in roads (SFX where possible) … this could be large cities along the reef, and it may happen sooner than we think. After all, sinkholes because of mining activity are nothing new, neither are tremors. There are around 25-40 000 Zama Zamas operating across a stretch of about 100km east to West. And we have seen the decay as a consequence of their activities happen all around us. …. It’s a highly visual piece with exploration of the entire world of Zama’s – from the massive threat that they now pose to infrastructure across the province through to the social (already covered by Chuma but to be touched on slightly) consequences, safety risks and the recent factional fighting in Riverlea. We look at the massive threat that uncontrolled mining could have on the city. - Underground tunnelling systems hollowing out Johannesburg. - Use of sewers and old tunnels to interconnect (beneath the gas pipelines) - The Zama shafts, quarries, and warrens, some right under major roads - The Sasol / FNB Study referencing the pipelines at FNB (still need to film the Zamas there) - A Geologist will say that it’s not the illicit gold that is the problem, it is the massive risk to infrastructure. - And we can show that the risk / danger is real. In a single 50sqm spot, at least 12 shafts were dug, in other areas, it’s beneath main thoroughfares. We can show how Eloff Street Extension wobbled because the ground below has become unstable… - Marius and Cobus (in rushes) will guide us with additional commentary, almost like guides along with the presenter, to the various Zama spots and into the sewers (up to a safe point). - Can we control/rein in the Zamas? With around 20 000 SAPS and Metro Police members across the province, law enforcement is outnumbered. But how did the Zamas become such a massive force? It’s the power of money. And a value chain that operates outside of the economy. - We will learn about the two major factions, the Basotho’s, and the Zulus. Their war (Riverlea is an example). - We see how Zamas surface mine and wash their loot. - We visit a Zama processing plant where pandukas process the raw washed rocks, grinds them into sand. And then packaged and sold on to the next tier in the chain. But we will speak to the Zimbabwean national who runs this operation, and he will reveal some of his clients and how his portion of the chain works. - The “sand” is then carted off to one of the many refineries on the East Rand… here it is mixed with legitimate gold and thus, “washed clean” and flows into the bullion system. A former manager at a refinery in Benoni will detail this for us. Also – who buys this gold? We endeavour to answer that question….. An independent Zama can produce up to 3g of gold a day, and dependent on the market price, can earn R 900 – R 1500 per gram. At 7 days a week and an average of 2g a day, it is a substantial amount. And apart from the money that the expats, many illegal, send home. They have spending power. And entire micro economies have grown around them. - The Zama Butchery and Braai, an open area where meat (cattle, bush meat etc) is grilled on old burning tyres. - The rows and rows of vendors selling Zama materials – from plastic buckets through to spades etc, - The entrepreneurs who make pandukas in industrial areas… The People - Marius and Cobus - “Smurf” – a Zama fixer - “Greg” – former refinery manager - Letwelo – Geologist at engineering firm Bulwark Consulting Engineers - “Brandon” – Zimbabwean second tier processor - Vox Pops with willing Zamas - Possible confront with Gold One (JSE), allegedly guilty of buying Zama gold. But I need to film the evidence of this if we can get close enough without being shot. metadata.Further information: ZAMA Treatment Visuals: I would like to create a highly visual, scary scenario at first, but bring in the absolute danger element with guns, lookouts, the sickening (see butchery) and then the gold that it becomes. I feel it must be fast paced, visually – and have a “blood diamonds” feel to it, for a lack of a better term… because in a sense, that is what this is becoming. And then… An introduction of buildings collapsing and giant gaping wounds in roads (SFX where possible) … this could be large cities along the reef, and it may happen sooner than we think. After all, sinkholes because of mining activity are nothing new, neither are tremors. There are around 25-40 000 Zama Zamas operating across a stretch of about 100km east to West. And we have seen the decay as a consequence of their activities happen all around us. …. It’s a highly visual piece with exploration of the entire world of Zama’s – from the massive threat that they now pose to infrastructure across the province through to the social (already covered by Chuma but to be touched on slightly) consequences, safety risks and the recent factional fighting in Riverlea. We look at the massive threat that uncontrolled mining could have on the city. - Underground tunnelling systems hollowing out Johannesburg. - Use of sewers and old tunnels to interconnect (beneath the gas pipelines) - The Zama shafts, quarries, and warrens, some right under major roads - The Sasol / FNB Study referencing the pipelines at FNB (still need to film the Zamas there) - A Geologist will say that it’s not the illicit gold that is the problem, it is the massive risk to infrastructure. - And we can show that the risk / danger is real. In a single 50sqm spot, at least 12 shafts were dug, in other areas, it’s beneath main thoroughfares. We can show how Eloff Street Extension wobbled because the ground below has become unstable… - Marius and Cobus (in rushes) will guide us with additional commentary, almost like guides along with the presenter, to the various Zama spots and into the sewers (up to a safe point). - Can we control/rein in the Zamas? With around 20 000 SAPS and Metro Police members across the province, law enforcement is outnumbered. But how did the Zamas become such a massive force? It’s the power of money. And a value chain that operates outside of the economy. - We will learn about the two major factions, the Basotho’s, and the Zulus. Their war (Riverlea is an example). - We see how Zamas surface mine and wash their loot. - We visit a Zama processing plant where pandukas process the raw washed rocks, grinds them into sand. And then packaged and sold on to the next tier in the chain. But we will speak to the Zimbabwean national who runs this operation, and he will reveal some of his clients and how his portion of the chain works. - The “sand” is then carted off to one of the many refineries on the East Rand… here it is mixed with legitimate gold and thus, “washed clean” and flows into the bullion system. A former manager at a refinery in Benoni will detail this for us. Also – who buys this gold? We endeavour to answer that question….. An independent Zama can produce up to 3g of gold a day, and dependent on the market price, can earn R 900 – R 1500 per gram. At 7 days a week and an average of 2g a day, it is a substantial amount. And apart from the money that the expats, many illegal, send home. They have spending power. And entire micro economies have grown around them. - The Zama Butchery and Braai, an open area where meat (cattle, bush meat etc) is grilled on old burning tyres. - The rows and rows of vendors selling Zama materials – from plastic buckets through to spades etc, - The entrepreneurs who make pandukas in industrial areas… The People - Marius and Cobus - “Smurf” – a Zama fixer - “Greg” – former refinery manager - Letwelo – Geologist at engineering firm Bulwark Consulting Engineers - “Brandon” – Zimbabwean second tier processor - Vox Pops with willing Zamas - Possible confront with Gold One (JSE), allegedly guilty of buying Zama gold. But I need to film the evidence of this if we can get close enough without being shot.
